title: Table Enhancements
summary: coordinate the delivered directive, table detail, managed table tools, and diagram detail sequence while retaining stopped default-entry and table-SVG proposals as decision records
content_html:
Table Enhancements

Status

Done. TE-1 — Directive Insertion, TE-2 — Table Detail View, and TE-3 — Managed Table Tools completed on 2026-08-03. TE-4 — Diagram Migration completed on 2026-08-04. TE-5 — Default Presentation and TE-6 — Table-to-SVG Publication stopped by explicit decision on 2026-08-04, closing the feature with four delivered outcomes and two retained stopped records.

Purpose

Table Enhancements coordinates the delivered table authoring and presentation path: insert optional source comments, mark a table for enhanced viewing, present it through the existing panel/view model, add Manage-only tools, and reuse the same detail view for diagrams.

The feature kept one sequence because source comments, the projected table marker, Content Detail View, table tools, and diagram migration are different stages of the same authoring-to-reading workflow. It extended existing Source, build, panel, view, and toolbar seams rather than creating a table application or parallel model. The stopped default-entry and SVG-publication proposals remain linked below as explicit decisions rather than implied future work.

Feature Documents

  • Authoring Directives Concept And Examples — delivered optional comment syntax, exact table-detail recognition, harmless no-op behavior, and the stopped table-publication consumer record.
  • Content Detail View Concept And Architecture — delivered static-source boundary, panel/view integration, expanded-main layout, target context, toolbar ownership, table experience, diagram reuse, and the stopped default-entry record.
  • TE-1 — Directive Insertion — add a Source-only Directives menu that inserts predefined source snippets without validating their build-time meaning.
  • TE-2 — Table Detail View — recognise the exact table-detail comment and deliver the public-safe static table view that consumes it.
  • TE-3 — Managed Table Tools — add resizable columns, Reset, and tab-delimited Copy table to the same view through Manage-owned contributions.
  • TE-4 — Diagram Migration — route persistent and rendered Mermaid diagrams into the same main view and make new-tab opening an optional view action.
  • TE-5 — Default Presentation — stopped proposal for flash-free initial Content Detail presentation.
  • TE-6 — Table-to-SVG Publication — stopped proposal for prepared linked-SVG public substitution.

Complete Feature Outcome

Manage Source has one Directives menu whose commands save the author from manually typing harmless source comments. Table Detail View recognises the exact correctly placed table-detail comment, projects its eligibility marker, and supplies the public-safe static table presentation. Unknown, malformed, misplaced, or unsupported comments remain invisible no-ops and never block a build; TE-1 does not attempt build-time validation.

The main panel can enter one expanded content-detail view for an exact presentation in the currently rendered document. Author-marked Markdown tables use natural-width columns capped by a readable wrapping default, sticky headers, a sticky first column, and unified horizontal and vertical scrolling. Manage contributes adjustable columns and tab-delimited Copy table without creating another viewer. Persistent SVG and inline Mermaid diagrams use the same view with their existing rendering and resource contracts.

The shipped Table to SVG source command remains a harmless insertion convenience whose comment renders as ordinary inert source text. Its proposed consumer and the proposed document-default entry path are retained only in the stopped TE-6 and TE-5 records.

Delivery Order

order delivery lifecycle outcome or decision
1 TE-1 — Directive Insertion ✅ Done The existing Source toolbar inserts either maintained optional comment as predefined source text.
2 TE-2 — Table Detail View ✅ Done The exact table-detail comment produces a public-safe static Content Detail presentation in public and Manage readers.
3 TE-3 — Managed Table Tools ✅ Done The same table view receives Manage-owned resizable columns, Reset, and tab-delimited Copy table without widening the public reader.
4 TE-4 — Diagram Migration ✅ Done Existing diagram detail controls enter the shared view; optional new-tab opening remains a toolbar action rather than the primary presentation model.
5 TE-5 — Default Presentation 🚫 Stopped The proposed flash-free document-default entry path will not proceed in this feature.
6 TE-6 — Table-to-SVG Publication 🚫 Stopped The proposed table-publication consumer will not proceed in this feature.

TE-1 is independently useful because it only inserts comments. TE-2 owns the complete comment-to-static-view outcome and establishes the public-safe target, layout, toolbar, return, and cleanup contracts. TE-3 adds Manage-only tools, and TE-4 reuses the completed view for diagrams. The accepted feature boundary ends there; TE-5 and TE-6 preserve the stopped decisions without extending the delivered product contract.

Boundary

Table Enhancements owns authoring conveniences and presentation for tables whose content remains owned by static document source. “Static” describes source ownership, not the rendering mechanism: an authored Mermaid fence may render dynamically and still qualify for the reused Content Detail view. Dynamic report lists, docs_subscope collections, search results, Recent, editors, spreadsheets, and generated application grids remain separate hosted or component views.

The feature does not add a central directive language, fourth panel, modal presentation framework, independent toolbar, detail route shell, spreadsheet editor, or generic widget registry. Panel Hosts and Control Surfaces remains the architecture authority; Toolbar Model remains the placement authority.

An unmarked table remains ordinary semantic HTML. table-detail supplies the marker consumed by Content Detail. The maintained table-publish snippet remains ordinary source text with harmless no-op behavior, as recorded by stopped TE-6. Canonical Markdown, working payloads, and transfer retain the semantic table and comments throughout.
